A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPMTrack and are readable throughout, including equations, tables and figures. v1 ends with references; v2 retains the main paper and adds Supplementary Material, Sections A-C. The available material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original tracking evaluations on seven datasets, component ablations in Tables 5-9, and attention visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds component and architectural experiments in Tables A.1-A.6, attribute comparisons and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed TMoE architecture, temporal-state propagation, token embeddings, losses and default prediction head are unchanged. These components already appear in v1. The supplement evaluates alternative heads and architectures as ablations and comparison controls.

E1.justification: The four training datasets and seven evaluation datasets are retained. Supplementary experiments use the existing GOT-10K, TrackingNet and LaSOT coverage, including previously represented tracking challenges. Alternative pretrained backbones change configurations, not task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table A.6 substantially expands Table 7's single conventional-MoE comparator with all-trainable, LoRA-tuned and sparse top-k alternatives. Figure A.2 also includes LoRAT-B378, ODTrack-B and ROMTrack-B384 in attribute comparisons, where Figure 4 did not include them. The original comparisons remain available.

E3.justification: Original splits, metrics, training budgets and inference settings remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce MAE/DropMAE backbones with patch size 16 and 192×192 reference/384×384 search images, plus prediction-head and expert-freezing/routing controls. These are settings for supplementary experiments, not revisions to the original evaluations.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds isolated target-state-token and token-type-embedding ablations, pretrained-backbone sensitivity, prediction-head comparisons and several conventional-MoE controls. Sections B-C add detailed attribute curves, challenging tracking case studies and visualizations of adjustment weights U. These substantially extend the questions investigated beyond v1's existing ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The supplementary results retain the original point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original numerical tables are unchanged, but Tables A.1-A.6 add substantial results. Examples include 76.3% GOT-10K AO without the target-state token, 76.8% AO with the convolutional head, and 74.4% LaSOT AUC for the LoRA-tuned conventional-MoE control versus TMoE's retained 74.9%. Figures A.2-A.4 add curves and qualitative findings for supplementary comparisons.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Equations 1-5 is unchanged. The supplement adds empirical analyses and explanations, with no new formal definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about TMoE, spatio-temporal tracking, parameter-efficient training and state-of-the-art performance. The supplement supplies additional support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: New interpretations connect foreground token embeddings and box-like adjustment weights to foreground discrimination. Appendix A.4 explains that the default MLP head is chosen for comparison fairness despite a better-performing alternative. A.5 explicitly cautions against extrapolating tracking results to language models and identifies sparse TMoE as unexplored.

D1.justification: The supplement documents added controls' pretrained FFN initialization, expert freezing, LoRA tuning and top-k activation, along with input resizing for patch-size-16 backbones. The original software, hardware, training recipe and source-code access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Eight references are added, including MAE and work on language-model reinforcement learning and MoE routing stability, supporting the appendix experiments and applicability discussion. The original related-work section and tracking contribution positioning are retained; other citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 adds a separately headed supplement with a roadmap and Sections A-C organizing further analyses and qualitative results. The original Sections 1-5 remain textually unchanged apart from citation numbering, so the narrative changes are confined to the supplementary extension.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables A.1-A.6 and Figures A.1-A.4, including conventional-MoE diagrams, a substantial grid of success/precision curves, tracking sequences and adjustment-weight heatmaps. These materially expand the visual presentation. Original figures and tables remain, while references move after the supplement.

improvement.justification: The supplement fills specific evidential gaps by isolating additional components and comparing TMoE with stronger conventional-MoE controls, while clarifying architectural choices and applicability limits. This improves support and interpretability. The overall gain is incremental because v1 already contains broad benchmark and core-ablation evidence, and the new small performance differences still lack uncertainty estimates.
